mainEntity.name: How much does a Mercedes Sprinter 211 or 317 CDI engine replacement cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: A rebuilt OM651 engine for the Sprinter 211 CDI costs £2,800-£3,800 supply-only; a rebuilt OM654 engine for the Sprinter 317 CDI costs £3,500-£5,400 supply-only. Supply-and-fit adds £450-£850 labour depending on complexity.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of timing chain failure on a Mercedes Sprinter 211 CDI?

acceptedAnswer.text: A rattling noise on cold start is the classic warning sign on the OM651 engine. The timing chain tensioner seal can leak oil (REC-005099 recall), causing chain slack and guide wear. If ignored, it can lead to catastrophic engine failure and significant commercial downtime.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of EGR failure on a Mercedes Sprinter 317 CDI?

acceptedAnswer.text: Reduced performance, increased fuel consumption, rough idling and dashboard warning lights are the classic warning signs on the OM654 engine. The low-pressure EGR valve and cooler can become clogged with soot over time, particularly on urban delivery cycles.

mainEntity.name: Is the Mercedes Sprinter 211 or 317 CDI engine reliable?

acceptedAnswer.text: The OM651 is fundamentally reliable - 200,000-300,000 km examples are common - but has predictable weak points: timing chain stretch from ~120,000 km, early Delphi injector failures, EGR clogging, and water pump leaks. The OM654 is a modern engine with improved efficiency but can suffer from low-pressure EGR clogging and DPF regeneration issues.

mainEntity.name: How long do Mercedes Sprinter 211 and 317 CDI engines last?

acceptedAnswer.text: Properly maintained OM651 engines routinely reach 150,000-200,000 miles before major work. Timing chain issues typically appear between 60,000-110,000 miles. The OM654 is too new for definitive long-term data but is showing good durability with regular servicing.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in my Mercedes Sprinter 211 or 317 CDI?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, if the Sprinter is otherwise in good condition with no structural rust or major transmission faults. A rebuilt OM651 costs £2,800-£3,800 - far less than replacing a £4,000-£12,000 vehicle. The OM654's higher value (£15,000-£35,000) makes replacement even more financially justifiable.

historyTimeline.h2: Mercedes Benz Sprinter 211/317 CDI - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The Sprinter 211 CDI and 317 CDI represent two distinct eras of Mercedes commercial diesel engineering. The 211 CDI launched with the W906 generation in 2006, powered by the OM651 2.1-litre four-cylinder diesel producing 114hp - a robust workhorse that defined the Sprinter range for over a decade. The 317 CDI arrived with the VS30 generation in 2018, powered by the OM654 2.0-litre four-cylinder diesel delivering 170hp - a modern, Euro 6 compliant engine with improved efficiency and reduced emissions. These engines represent the evolution of the Sprinter diesel line from the proven OM651 to the advanced OM654 architecture.

commonProblems.h2: Mercedes Sprinter 211/317 CDI Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The Sprinter 211 CDI's OM651 and the 317 CDI's OM654 are both robust commercial diesel engines, but each has well-documented weaknesses that can lead to significant repair costs. The OM651's single most critical failure point is timing chain stretch from approximately 120,000 km , while the OM654 is prone to low-pressure EGR valve clogging and DPF regeneration issues. Every rebuilt engine supplied through EnginesMarket includes upgraded components addressing these original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.group: OM651 Timing Chain Tensioner Seal Leak
problems.h4: OM651 Timing Chain Tensioner Seal Leak - The Most Critical Sprinter Diesel Failure
problems.rootCause: The seal ring between the timing chain tensioner and the engine may leak oil due to manufacturing tolerances . This allows oil to escape, leading to loss of oil pressure, chain slack, and potential guide rail breakage . Over 100,000 vehicles with the OM651 engine were recalled globally . The OM651's single most critical failure point is timing chain stretch from approximately 120,000 km . A cold-start rattling noise is the classic warning sign . If the chain jumps a tooth, the consequences range from misfires and cam/crank correlation codes to catastrophic engine damage .

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Head removal, valve inspection, guide replacement after chain jump
repairOptions.longevity: Only viable if bottom end is undamaged; high labour cost

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical 2006-2018 Sprinter 211 CDI is worth approximately £4,000-£12,000 depending on generation, mileage and condition. A rebuilt OM651 engine costing £2,800-£3,800 typically extends vehicle life by 80,000-120,000 miles, making replacement significantly more economical than purchasing a new or used replacement van.
problems.recommendation: On a revenue-generating Sprinter, we strongly advise checking your VIN for recall REC-005099 immediately . If the recall work has been performed but cold-start rattling persists, a preventative timing chain kit at specialist rates (£1,200-£1,800) is the most cost-effective intervention if caught early. Once the chain has jumped or metal debris contaminates the sump, a full rebuilt OM651 exchange unit is the only financially viable route to avoid repeat failures and minimise commercial downtime. The OM651 is fundamentally reliable - 200,000-300,000 km examples are common - but timing chain issues are predictable and manageable with the right maintenance schedule .

problems.h4: OM651 Injector Seal Failure (Black Death) - Carbon Build-Up That Destroys Cylinder Heads
problems.rootCause: The OM651's injector seals can fail over time, allowing high-pressure combustion gases to blow past the injector. The leaking gases bake into a hard, tar-like carbon crust around the injector - "Black Death". Early Delphi piezo injectors (pre-2012) are particularly prone to failure . Left long enough, the injector becomes welded into the head. Carbon buildup leads to compression loss, rough running, and eventual cylinder head damage.

repairOptions.longevity: Effective if caught early before injector seizes

problems.recommendation: Injector seal leaks on the OM651 are common but manageable. If you notice diesel fumes in the cabin or see carbon buildup around the injectors, have a specialist inspect the seals immediately. Caught early, resealing an injector is a £150-£250 job. The 220 CDI and 250 CDI variants were equipped with Piezo injectors which became known for their high susceptibility to failure . On a commercial Sprinter worth £4,000-£12,000, preventative injector seal replacement is always the better investment.

problems.h4: OM654 Low-Pressure EGR Valve Clogging - The 317 CDI's Emissions Challenge
problems.rootCause: The low-pressure EGR cooler housing on OM654 units features complex internal baffles that trap soot rapidly under urban stop-start conditions. Coolant and exhaust gases mix when internal cracks develop, causing immediate DPF blockage and engine control unit fault codes. This is a systemic design vulnerability rather than isolated wear on VS30 generation vans.

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical 2018-present Sprinter 317 CDI is worth approximately £15,000-£35,000 depending on generation, mileage and condition. These modern Euro 6 vans retain strong values, making engine replacement a justifiable investment for commercial operators.
problems.recommendation: On newer Sprinter VS30 models, EGR clogging is a systemic design vulnerability rather than isolated wear. problems.rootCause: DPF regeneration issues are common on OM654 engines used primarily for short urban journeys. The DPF requires sustained motorway speeds to reach regeneration temperature. Turbocharger actuator faults can also cause boost loss and reduced performance. The OM654 features twin-turbocharging for improved response and efficiency .
